subject: chemistry-hl
about: Original practice questions written for NevaIB from the IB guide's syllabus understandings and the school's unit order. Not IB past-paper questions, not publisher material and not IB markschemes: the marking points are written for self-marking. Organisms, experiments and data in data-response items are invented for practice.

items.stem: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon produces:
items.note: With enough oxygen, all C → CO₂ and all H → H₂O.

items.stem: Incomplete combustion is a problem mainly because it:
choices: Releases more energy than complete combustion
Produces toxic carbon monoxide and soot
Uses up more oxygen than complete combustion
Produces only water vapour as waste
items.note: CO binds to haemoglobin; soot (C) damages lungs. Less energy is released per mole of fuel.
Coal, crude oil and natural gas formed over millions of years. The others are renewable biofuels.

items.stem: What is the balanced equation for the complete combustion of propane?
Biofuels are described as renewable because:
choices: They release no carbon dioxide when they burn
They have a higher specific energy than petrol
They do not need any land or water to produce
The plants they come from can be regrown in a short time
items.note: CO₂ released was recently absorbed by photosynthesis; they are not carbon-neutral overall because of farming and processing.

items.stem: Specific energy is the energy released per:
items.note: Specific energy (kJ kg⁻¹) is per mass; energy density is per volume.

items.stem: The enthalpy of combustion of methane is −891 kJ mol⁻¹ (M = 16.05 g mol⁻¹). Its specific energy is about:
Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas because its molecules:
choices: Absorb ultraviolet radiation from the Sun
Reflect visible light back into space
Absorb infrared radiation re-emitted by the Earth
Destroy ozone in the upper atmosphere
items.note: Bond vibrations in CO₂ absorb IR emitted by the warm Earth, then re-emit it, warming the lower atmosphere.

items.stem: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell with an acidic electrolyte, the reaction at the anode is:
items.note: Oxidation at the anode: hydrogen loses electrons. Oxygen is reduced at the cathode.

items.stem: Compared with petrol, ethanol releases less energy per gram when burned mainly because:
choices: It is already partly oxidised, as it contains oxygen
It is a liquid rather than a gas
It produces more water per mole
items.note: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) contains an O atom; less energy is released as fewer bonds to O are formed per gram.

items.stem: Which reason best explains why the efficiency of electricity from a fuel cell can exceed that from burning the same fuel in a power station?
choices: The fuel cell releases more energy per mole of fuel
The fuel cell uses a catalyst that increases ΔH
Chemical energy is converted directly to electrical energy, with less heat loss
The fuel cell produces no products at all
items.note: Power stations convert chemical → heat → kinetic → electrical, losing heat at each step.

items.stem: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of using coal and natural gas as fuels.
markscheme: Coal: more abundant/cheaper in many places (1)
Coal releases more CO₂ per unit energy, plus SO₂ and particulates (1)
Natural gas: burns more cleanly, less CO₂ per unit energy (1)
items.tactic: Balance: at least one point for and against each fuel.

items.stem: Write equations for the incomplete combustion of methane to form (a) carbon monoxide and (b) carbon.
items.tactic: Balance O last; incomplete combustion uses less oxygen per mole of fuel.

items.stem: Explain why biofuels are not completely carbon-neutral.
markscheme: CO₂ released on burning was absorbed in photosynthesis (so partly neutral) (1)
Fossil fuels are used in farming, fertiliser production, transport and processing (1)
Land-use change (e.g. deforestation) releases additional CO₂ (1)
items.tactic: Evaluate: state the neutral argument, then what it misses.

items.stem:
Data response. Specific energies of four fuels (kJ g⁻¹, calculated from enthalpies of combustion) and CO₂ released per kJ (mg kJ⁻¹): hydrogen 141, 0; methane 55.5, 49.4; octane 47.9, 64.4; ethanol 29.7, 64.4.
(a) Calculate the mass of octane needed to release 1000 kJ. (b) Which fuel releases the least CO₂ per kJ among the carbon-based fuels? (c) Suggest two reasons why hydrogen is not yet widely used in cars despite its high specific energy.
markscheme: (c) Hydrogen is a gas with low energy density, so needs high-pressure storage (1)
Mostly produced from fossil fuels / lack of refuelling infrastructure / safety (flammability) (1)
items.tactic: Data questions: quote the values you use, with units, and name the fuel in your answer.
